payload.rationale: Dune: Part Three (Warner Bros./Legendary, dir. Denis Villeneuve) has been dated for December 18, 2026, with principal photography completed in 2025 and a premium-format (IMAX 70mm) rollout planned. The main known risk to that date is the direct collision with Avengers: Doomsday, which Disney moved onto the same December 18, 2026 slot, creating pressure on one of the studios to move. Historically, when two tentpoles share a date, one often relocates, but such shifts typically occur many months in advance, not in the final quarter when marketing campaigns, exhibitor bookings, and premium-screen commitments are locked. With the forecast cutoff on September 19, 2026 (about 13 weeks before release), a delay not already announced would be unusual absent a production/post-production crisis or a broader disruption. Base rates for a wide-release studio tentpole slipping its date within the last three months are low (roughly 5-10%). I add some weight for the unusual date clash and the possibility that a move was announced between my knowledge horizon and the cutoff that I cannot observe. Too high: if the film is finished, tracking well, and WB has repeatedly reaffirmed the date, a late move is very improbable (~5%). Too low: if a move had already been announced (e.g., earlier in 2026 to escape Doomsday or to secure IMAX screens), the event would already be effectively YES, which no supplied evidence lets me rule out; also unforeseen post-production, labor, or corporate (WB ownership/merger) issues could force a shift.
limitations: No current research or news supplied; status as of September 2026 is unknown.
Cannot verify whether a date change was announced after my knowledge horizon.
Contract nuances (e.g., limited/premium early screenings vs. wide release, partial-day shifts) unknown.
Estimate relies on general base rates for late tentpole date changes.
